what_it_means: The money taken in for contracts sold in the period, before any of it counts as earned.
why_shown_this_way: A monthly total, because each month's sales stand on their own.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much business came in; leaders use it to set dealer targets and size the reserve.

what_it_means: The part of the premium used up as coverage time passes; a 36-month contract earns a slice each month.
why_shown_this_way: A line over time, because earning builds slowly and the trend matters more than one month.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the bottom half of the loss ratio, so it decides whether a book looks profitable.
decision_it_drives: Whether a book is judged profitable

what_it_means: Claims already paid plus money held for claims that are filed but not paid yet.
why_shown_this_way: Shown next to earned premium so you can see what came in against what went out.
why_your_boss_asks: Partners who share the risk ask for it to see whether their book makes money.
decision_it_drives: Renew, re-price or re-train a dealer

what_it_means: For every $1 of premium earned, how many cents went to claims.
why_shown_this_way: A percent, so a big book and a small book can be compared fairly.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether a dealer's program is renewed, re-priced or re-trained.
decision_it_drives: Renew, re-price or re-train a dealer

what_it_means: Premium earned over the last 12 months, added together.
why_shown_this_way: A rolling 12-month total smooths out busy and slow months.
why_your_boss_asks: Leaders compare it with last year to see whether the book is growing.

what_it_means: Claims paid plus money held for open claims, over the last 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: A rolling 12-month total, so one heavy month does not hide the trend.
why_your_boss_asks: The top half of the 12-month loss ratio used in dealer and partner reviews.

what_it_means: Claims divided by earned premium for the last 12 months combined.
why_shown_this_way: Twelve months together, so one bad month does not swing the number.
why_your_boss_asks: Used in dealer and partner reviews to decide on pricing and who keeps a share of the risk.

what_it_means: How many claims each contract makes per year of coverage.
why_shown_this_way: Per year of coverage, so a big book and a small book compare fairly.
why_your_boss_asks: A rise means prices may be too low or cars are riskier; it drives re-pricing.

what_it_means: The number of claims accepted for review, leaving out denied ones.
why_shown_this_way: A plain count; it is the top half of how often contracts claim.
why_your_boss_asks: Claims managers plan adjuster staffing from it.

what_it_means: Coverage time counted in contract-years; one contract active all year counts as 1.
why_shown_this_way: Used as the bottom half of claim frequency, so book size does not distort it.
why_your_boss_asks: Lets leaders compare claim rates fairly between big and small dealers.

what_it_means: How many claims received a payment.
why_shown_this_way: A plain count per month.
why_your_boss_asks: Claims managers use it for workload and cash planning.

what_it_means: Total dollars paid out on claims.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month, because cash goes out month by month.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance plans cash from it; partners compare it with the reserve set aside.

what_it_means: The average amount paid on each paid claim.
why_shown_this_way: An average in dollars, so rising repair costs show up quickly.
why_your_boss_asks: Rising averages point to parts and labor costs; they drive rate changes.

what_it_means: How many contracts dealers sold.
why_shown_this_way: A count per month, so busy and slow months are easy to see.
why_your_boss_asks: Drives sales targets, dealer coaching and commission.

what_it_means: How many sold contracts were later cancelled, for example when the car was sold or paid off.
why_shown_this_way: A count, next to contracts sold.
why_your_boss_asks: High cancels cut income and trigger dealer chargebacks; it drives retraining.

what_it_means: Of the contracts sold in a period, the share that has cancelled so far.
why_shown_this_way: Grouped by sale date, so each group is followed over its own life; recent groups look low.
why_your_boss_asks: Buyers and partners ask how long contracts stay on the books; it affects pricing and bids.

what_it_means: Contracts sold in the accounting month; a change to an old contract adds nothing.
why_shown_this_way: A count per month and product family.
why_your_boss_asks: The monthly production check for each dealer and territory.
decision_it_drives: Which dealer to call and coach

what_it_means: What dealers owe the administrator for the contracts they sold this period.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month, before any cancels.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the cash that must arrive to fund fees, insurance and the claims reserve.

what_it_means: What customers paid the dealer for the contracts sold.
why_shown_this_way: A money total, shown next to dealer cost.
why_your_boss_asks: Compared with dealer cost to see what the store earns on each sale.

what_it_means: The contract price entered by the dealer for contracts sold in the period.
why_shown_this_way: A money total, so stores of one group can be compared.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealer groups compare what each store charges to set pricing guidance.

what_it_means: The average dealer cost per contract sold.
why_shown_this_way: An average, so a shift toward richer or cheaper coverage is easy to spot.
why_your_boss_asks: Product managers use it in pricing reviews.

what_it_means: Retail price minus dealer cost: what the store keeps on contracts it sold.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealer groups compare markup across stores to set a pricing policy.

what_it_means: Contracts active right now, counted at month end.
why_shown_this_way: A month-end balance, so months are never added together.
why_your_boss_asks: States and buyers ask for the size of the active book; it backs every yearly filing.

what_it_means: Premium collected for coverage time that has not happened yet; part is owed back if contracts cancel.
why_shown_this_way: A month-end balance.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance checks it against the reserve held; buyers use it to value the book.

what_it_means: Cancel transactions posted in the month.
why_shown_this_way: A count per accounting month.
why_your_boss_asks: Plans refund cash and cancel-desk workload.

what_it_means: Cancels that were not later reversed by a reinstatement.
why_shown_this_way: A count; reversed cancels are left out so they are not counted twice.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the true cancel count behind cancel rates and refunds.

what_it_means: Cancels that stuck, leaving out cancels that only fixed a data-entry mistake.
why_shown_this_way: A count; a correction is a fix, not a customer leaving.
why_your_boss_asks: Bids and partners ask how the cancel rate is worked out; this is the cleaner count.

what_it_means: Customer cancels this period divided by contracts written, without data-entry fixes.
why_shown_this_way: A percent per period, shown next to the rate that keeps corrections in.
why_your_boss_asks: A buyer may ask for both methods; it shows how sticky the book really is.

what_it_means: Money paid back to customers when their contract cancelled.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance plans cash from it and checks refunds follow each contract's refund rule.

what_it_means: The fee kept when a customer cancels, as the contract allows.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month.
why_your_boss_asks: Part of program income; checked on dealer statements.

what_it_means: Money taken back from the dealer on a cancelled contract, for the part not yet earned.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month.
why_your_boss_asks: Settles what each dealer owes back on the monthly statement.

what_it_means: The part of dealer cost returned when contracts cancel.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month.
why_your_boss_asks: It explains part of the gap between two reserve reports.

what_it_means: Cancels that stuck this period divided by contracts written in the same period.
why_shown_this_way: A period view, so it can be read the month it happens.
why_your_boss_asks: An early warning for a dealer whose customers cancel quickly.

what_it_means: Dealer cost written minus dealer cost refunded on cancels.
why_shown_this_way: A money total for the period.
why_your_boss_asks: The real income base for the period; it ties to the books.

what_it_means: Cancelled contracts that were turned back on.
why_shown_this_way: A count per month.
why_your_boss_asks: They change dealer statements and refunds, so finance tracks them.

what_it_means: Reinstatements that were later reversed.
why_shown_this_way: A count per month.
why_your_boss_asks: A data and settlement check: each one changes what a dealer is owed.

what_it_means: Claim dollars paid, counted in the accounting month they were booked.
why_shown_this_way: By accounting month, so it ties to the books.
why_your_boss_asks: Statements and state filings must use the booked figure.

what_it_means: Claims paid plus the change in money held for open claims, by accounting month.
why_shown_this_way: By accounting month, so it ties to the books.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the top half of the booked loss ratio on partner statements.

plain_name: Change in money held for open claims
what_it_means: How much the money held for open claims went up or down this month.
why_shown_this_way: A monthly change, up or down.
why_your_boss_asks: A big jump means large claims are open; finance checks the reserve is enough.

what_it_means: Claims that had any payment or reserve change booked this month.
why_shown_this_way: A count per month.
why_your_boss_asks: Claims managers use it for adjuster workload.

plain_name: Average days to process a claim
what_it_means: Average days from a claim's first entry to its booked payment.
why_shown_this_way: An average in days, against the service target.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the service promise to dealers and customers; it drives staffing.

what_it_means: New claims reported in the month.
why_shown_this_way: A count by the month reported.
why_your_boss_asks: Plans staffing and warns early of a rise in breakdowns.

what_it_means: Claims counted by the month the car broke down, from both admin systems.
why_shown_this_way: By breakdown month; recent months still grow as late claims arrive.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the base for the denial rate and the early-claim checks.

what_it_means: Claims not paid because the repair was not covered.
why_shown_this_way: A count by breakdown month.
why_your_boss_asks: States ask for denied claims on the yearly renewal; a spike triggers a review.

what_it_means: Claims closed with a payment, counted by breakdown month.
why_shown_this_way: A count; it is the bottom half of the average paid claim.
why_your_boss_asks: Used to track repair cost per claim over time.

what_it_means: Total paid on claims that were paid, by breakdown month.
why_shown_this_way: A money total; it is the top half of the average paid claim.
why_your_boss_asks: Used to track repair cost per claim over time.

what_it_means: Claims not yet closed on the report date.
why_shown_this_way: A count on one date.
why_your_boss_asks: The daily adjuster workload.

what_it_means: Open claims that were reported more than 30 days ago.
why_shown_this_way: A count with an age cut, so the follow-up list is clear.
why_your_boss_asks: Old open claims mean unhappy customers; managers assign follow-ups from it.

what_it_means: Average days from a claim being reported to being closed.
why_shown_this_way: An average in days, against the service target.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the service promise; it drives staffing and dealer satisfaction.

what_it_means: Deductibles customers paid on claims.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per month.
why_your_boss_asks: It lowers net claim cost; finance checks it against contract terms.

what_it_means: Of all reported claims, the share that was denied.
why_shown_this_way: A percent by breakdown month, so a change in rules shows up.
why_your_boss_asks: Too high draws complaints and state attention; too low can mean loose checks.

what_it_means: Paid dollars divided by paid claims; the same claims are on top and bottom.
why_shown_this_way: An average in dollars by breakdown month.
why_your_boss_asks: Tracks repair cost inflation; it drives rate reviews.

what_it_means: For every $1 set aside to pay claims, how much was paid or is owed on claims.
why_shown_this_way: A percent by accounting month, so it ties to the books.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether a dealer's reinsurance company can take a distribution.

what_it_means: How much of the claims reserve has been earned so far, as a share of all reserve written.
why_shown_this_way: A gauge, because it shows how far through their life the contracts are.
why_your_boss_asks: A low earned % means a young book whose loss ratio will still rise; partners ask before deciding.

what_it_means: Share of contracts written that cancelled and stayed cancelled.
why_shown_this_way: A gauge next to earned % and loss ratio.
why_your_boss_asks: Part of every experience review with a dealer or partner.

what_it_means: Money dealers sent to pay for the contracts they sold.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: It funds the reserve; finance ties it to the bank.

what_it_means: Payments received from dealers.
why_shown_this_way: A count per period.
why_your_boss_asks: Billing workload, and the base for the late rate.

what_it_means: Dealer payments that arrived more than 30 days after the contract was entered.
why_shown_this_way: A count over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: Late money means the reserve is funded late; it triggers late fees and calls.

what_it_means: Fees billed to dealers for paying late, a set share of the late amount.
why_shown_this_way: A money total over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: Program income and a nudge to pay on time; billed on the dealer statement.

what_it_means: Average days from contract entry to the dealer's money arriving.
why_shown_this_way: An average in days, against the 30-day standard.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which dealers to call about payment habits.

what_it_means: Of all dealer payments, the share that arrived late.
why_shown_this_way: A percent, so dealers of any size compare fairly.
why_your_boss_asks: Over half late puts a dealer on watch and starts collection calls.

what_it_means: Dealer cost divided into its parts: admin fee, insurer fee, tax, commission and reserves.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per part.
why_your_boss_asks: Each part goes to a different party, so every settlement needs it right.

what_it_means: The part of dealer cost put aside to pay future claims.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the money behind the contracts; states and partners check it.

what_it_means: The part of dealer cost held for the dealer's later share of profit.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: Sizes what may be paid back to dealers later.

what_it_means: All parts of dealer cost that have been earned in the period, as coverage time passed.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month total with a small trend line.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the bottom half of the combined ratio on the profit and loss statement.

what_it_means: The part of the claims reserve earned this period as coverage time passes.
why_shown_this_way: A money total with a small trend line.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the bottom half of the loss ratio on partner statements.

what_it_means: The administrator's fee, counted as it is earned over the contract term.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: The administrator's own income line.

what_it_means: Commission, insurer fee and premium tax, counted as they are earned.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: Part of the combined ratio: the cost of selling the book.

what_it_means: Claims plus selling costs plus the admin fee, divided by earned premium; over 100% the book lost money.
why_shown_this_way: A percent with a 100% break-even line.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether a product or program is priced right overall.

what_it_means: Claims reported on one dealer's contracts.
why_shown_this_way: A count over the last 12 months.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the base for that dealer's early-claim check.

what_it_means: Claims where the car broke down soon after the contract started.
why_shown_this_way: A count for the headline window.
why_your_boss_asks: Too many can mean cars were sold with problems already; it triggers a dealer review.

what_it_means: Of all reported claims, the share that came soon after the start date.
why_shown_this_way: A percent, so dealers of any size compare fairly.
why_your_boss_asks: A high share can mean problem cars or a waiting period not enforced; it starts a review.

what_it_means: Dealers that break at least one watch rule: high loss ratio, late payment or early claims.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with the full list below.
why_your_boss_asks: It is this month's call list for dealer relations.

what_it_means: Dealers whose 12-month loss ratio is over the watch line, among dealers with enough volume.
why_shown_this_way: A count of dealers, not a percent, so it reads as a to-do list.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides which dealers to re-price, retrain or review with their reinsurance company.
decision_it_drives: Re-price, retrain or review a dealer

what_it_means: Contracts one dealer wrote in the months shown.
why_shown_this_way: A count over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: The production check for each dealer.

what_it_means: Of one dealer's contracts written in the months shown, how many have cancelled since.
why_shown_this_way: A count, grouped by sale month.
why_your_boss_asks: The top half of the dealer's cancel rate.

what_it_means: The claims reserve one dealer's contracts earned in the months shown.
why_shown_this_way: A money total over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: The bottom half of the dealer's loss ratio; small totals are not judged.

what_it_means: Claims paid and held on one dealer's contracts, by breakdown month.
why_shown_this_way: A money total over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: The top half of the dealer's loss ratio.

what_it_means: Payments one dealer sent in the months shown.
why_shown_this_way: A count over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: The bottom half of the dealer's late payment rate.

what_it_means: Payments from one dealer that arrived late.
why_shown_this_way: A count over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: The top half of the dealer's late payment rate.

what_it_means: All the days late added up across one dealer's late payments.
why_shown_this_way: A total; the average days late is built from it.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how late, not just how often, a dealer pays.

what_it_means: For one dealer, claims divided by the claims reserve its contracts earned.
why_shown_this_way: A percent over the last 12 months, against a watch line.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether the dealer's reinsurance company can take a distribution, or needs a review.

what_it_means: Of one dealer's contracts written in the months shown, the share since cancelled.
why_shown_this_way: A percent by sale month.
why_your_boss_asks: High cancels mean chargebacks and lost income; it drives retraining.

what_it_means: Of one dealer's payments, the share that arrived late.
why_shown_this_way: A percent over the last 12 months.
why_your_boss_asks: Over half late puts the dealer on watch.

what_it_means: For late payments only, the average number of days late.
why_shown_this_way: An average in days.
why_your_boss_asks: Separates a dealer that is a few days late from one that is months late.

what_it_means: Where this dealer's loss ratio sits among peers; a high number means worse than most.
why_shown_this_way: A rank from 0 to 100, shown for one dealer only.
why_your_boss_asks: Lets a dealer see how it compares without seeing other dealers' numbers.

what_it_means: The loss ratio of similar dealers' VSC contracts, as one average; no single dealer can be picked out.
why_shown_this_way: One percent next to yours, so the gap is easy to see.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows a dealer whether its claims run high for its kind of store before a review is called.

what_it_means: The reserve the state's formula says the company must hold.
why_shown_this_way: A money figure for each state, on the state's own basis.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether the state filing is accepted, so the company can keep selling there.

what_it_means: The reserve the company actually holds for contracts in that state.
why_shown_this_way: A money figure next to the required reserve.
why_your_boss_asks: If it is below the required reserve, money must be moved before filing.

what_it_means: How much the reserve held falls short of what the state requires; 0 is the goal.
why_shown_this_way: A money figure; any amount above 0 is flagged.
why_your_boss_asks: A shortfall must be funded before the filing is sent.

what_it_means: Customer complaints received in the filing period.
why_shown_this_way: A count per filing window; windows are never added together.
why_your_boss_asks: States ask for it on the yearly renewal.

what_it_means: One numbered answer on a state form, such as contracts in force at year end.
why_shown_this_way: One number per line, scope and basis.
why_your_boss_asks: Every line must be right for the filing to be accepted.

what_it_means: Commission paid to agents for contracts sold.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: Agent payouts and the cost of selling.

what_it_means: Commission paid to an agent before it is earned; it is worked off as contracts earn.
why_shown_this_way: A money total per period.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance tracks how much could be owed back if contracts cancel.

what_it_means: Claims already reported on contracts sold so far, paid or still open.
why_shown_this_way: A money total at the valuation date.
why_your_boss_asks: The known part of what the book will cost; the rest is estimated.

what_it_means: Money for claims that have happened but nobody has reported yet.
why_shown_this_way: A money estimate from how past claims arrived late.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance books it so the loss ratio is not too rosy; partners ask before any distribution.

plain_name: Losses still to come on active contracts
what_it_means: Expected claims on coverage time not used yet, paid for out of unearned premium.
why_shown_this_way: A money estimate at the valuation date.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows whether the unearned premium is enough for the claims still ahead.

what_it_means: Reported losses plus IBNR plus losses still to come: what the book should cost in the end.
why_shown_this_way: A money total; the three parts add up to it.
why_your_boss_asks: The figure pricing and reserve decisions rest on.

what_it_means: Ultimate losses divided by the premium that pays for them.
why_shown_this_way: A percent per sale group, against a 100% line.
why_your_boss_asks: Groups above the line will lose money for their reinsurance company; it drives re-pricing.

what_it_means: The date the estimates were calculated on.
why_shown_this_way: A date, so you know how fresh the estimates are.
why_your_boss_asks: Every reserve figure is quoted as of a date; partners ask which one.

what_it_means: The loss ratio changes with how fast premium is counted as earned.
why_shown_this_way: Three lines on one chart, so the effect of the earning rule is plain.
why_your_boss_asks: Picking the earning rule changes reported profit; finance and partners must agree on it.

plain_name: Reported losses and IBNR by sale group
what_it_means: For contracts sold in each quarter: claims reported, claims expected but not reported, and claims still to come.
why_shown_this_way: Stacked bars, so the parts add up to the expected total.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which sale groups still carry most of their cost ahead of them.

plain_name: Ultimate loss ratio by sale group
what_it_means: Where each sale quarter is expected to land once every claim is in.
why_shown_this_way: Bars against a 100% line, so losing groups stand out.
why_your_boss_asks: Groups above the line will lose money for their reinsurance company.

plain_name: Claims reported per month by coverage level
what_it_means: How many claims arrive each month, split by how much the contract covers.
why_shown_this_way: Lines over time; the last months dip because some claims are not reported yet.
why_your_boss_asks: Claims managers plan staffing; the dip shows why IBNR is needed.

what_it_means: Losses for each sale quarter, as that quarter's contracts get older.
why_shown_this_way: A triangle table: read across a row to see losses pile up with age.
why_your_boss_asks: Actuaries use it to estimate IBNR; partners ask to see it before a distribution.

plain_name: Dealer cost written vs earned premium
what_it_means: Money written when contracts are sold, against the slower amount earned over their terms.
why_shown_this_way: Three lines over time, because earning trails writing by years.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much future earning is already locked in; leaders use it for planning.

what_it_means: Claims as a share of the earned claims reserve, and all costs as a share of earned premium.
why_shown_this_way: Two lines with a 100% break-even line.
why_your_boss_asks: Over 100% combined means the book lost money; it drives pricing and program reviews.

what_it_means: How many contracts are active at each month end.
why_shown_this_way: A line, because the active book grows or shrinks slowly.
why_your_boss_asks: A growing line means sales beat expiries and cancels; buyers and states ask for it.

what_it_means: Of contracts sold in each quarter, the share cancelled so far.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per sale quarter; recent quarters look low because they had less time to cancel.
why_your_boss_asks: Buyers and partners ask how long contracts stay on the books.

what_it_means: The ten dealers paying out the largest share of their earned claims reserve in claims.
why_shown_this_way: A short ranked table, only dealers with enough volume to judge.
why_your_boss_asks: The dealers to review first; it decides re-pricing, retraining or a partner review.

plain_name: Loss ratio by coverage level and term
what_it_means: How much of its earned claims reserve each product group pays out in claims.
why_shown_this_way: Bars by coverage level and contract length, so the worst group stands out.
why_your_boss_asks: Product managers use it to re-price the weakest coverage and term mix.

what_it_means: The loss ratio on new cars against used cars.
why_shown_this_way: Two bars side by side.
why_your_boss_asks: Older cars break down more; it supports a higher price on used cars.

what_it_means: How many claims a contract files per year, for each coverage level.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per coverage level.
why_your_boss_asks: Broader coverage claims more often; it checks the price steps between levels.

what_it_means: The average paid claim for each coverage level.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per coverage level.
why_your_boss_asks: Checks that richer coverage is priced for its bigger claims.

what_it_means: Every product by new or used vehicle, with its key results.
why_shown_this_way: A full table behind show more, for people who need every row.
why_your_boss_asks: Product managers check one product without asking for a report.

what_it_means: Claim cost over the last 12 months, split by type of repair.
why_shown_this_way: Bars sorted largest first, because a few repair types drive most of the cost.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows where coverage terms or prices need attention.

what_it_means: Each dealer's claims as a share of the claims reserve it earned in the last 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: One bar per dealer with a dotted watch line.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealers past the line go on the loss-ratio watch.

what_it_means: Every dealer, with a link to its own packet of reports.
why_shown_this_way: A list, so you can open one dealer quickly.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealer relations open one packet before a dealer call.

what_it_means: Claims per year of coverage, by the month the car broke down.
why_shown_this_way: A line over time; the latest months rise as late claims arrive.
why_your_boss_asks: A rising line means each contract claims more; it drives re-pricing.

plain_name: Average claim and denial rate by month
what_it_means: The average paid claim, and the share of claims denied, by breakdown month.
why_shown_this_way: Two lines on two scales, because they move for different reasons.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows repair cost trends and whether claim rules changed.

plain_name: Early claims by days after the start
what_it_means: Claims where the car broke down within a set number of days of the contract start.
why_shown_this_way: Bars by window; each bar includes the shorter windows.
why_your_boss_asks: Too many early claims can mean problem cars at sale; it starts a dealer review.

what_it_means: The parts that cost the most in claims, parts plus labor.
why_shown_this_way: Bars sorted largest first.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which repairs to watch when setting coverage and prices.

what_it_means: The same claim results, split by product.
why_shown_this_way: A table; ratios are rebuilt from totals, never averaged.
why_your_boss_asks: Product managers compare products on the same rules.

what_it_means: Claims still open today, grouped by days since they were reported.
why_shown_this_way: Bars by age band; 30 days or older needs a follow-up.
why_your_boss_asks: Managers assign follow-ups so customers are not left waiting.

what_it_means: Dealers that sold at least one contract in the last 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: A count over the window.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how wide the selling network is; bids and sales plans use it.

what_it_means: The product dealers sold most in the last 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: One name, so the main product is clear at a glance.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows where production depends on one product.

plain_name: Contracts written per month by product family
what_it_means: How many contracts dealers sold each month, split by product family.
why_shown_this_way: Stacked bars per month, so total and mix show together.
why_your_boss_asks: The monthly production check; managers spot a family that is slipping.

what_it_means: Contracts each of the top 25 dealers wrote in each product over 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: A grid, so gaps in a dealer's product mix stand out.
why_your_boss_asks: Field reps use it to pitch the products a dealer does not sell yet.

what_it_means: Contracts sold but not finished: paperwork or payment is still missing.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with the oldest ones listed below.
why_your_boss_asks: The dealer must finish them so customers are really covered.

what_it_means: How many dealers have at least one unfinished contract.
why_shown_this_way: A count of dealers.
why_your_boss_asks: The call list for dealer services today.

what_it_means: The middle number of days contracts have been waiting; half wait less, half longer.
why_shown_this_way: A middle value, so a few very old contracts do not distort it.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows whether paperwork is slowing down across dealers.

what_it_means: Unfinished contracts waiting more than 60 days.
why_shown_this_way: A count with an age cut.
why_your_boss_asks: These customers may think they are covered when they are not; call first.

what_it_means: What customers paid for contracts still unfinished.
why_shown_this_way: A money total.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the income held up by unfinished paperwork.

what_it_means: How long sold contracts have been waiting for the dealer.
why_shown_this_way: Bars by age band, oldest on the right.
why_your_boss_asks: Old pending contracts are customers at risk; it sets who to chase first.

plain_name: Dealers with the most pending contracts
what_it_means: Dealers with many or very old unfinished contracts.
why_shown_this_way: A ranked table, so the first call is at the top.
why_your_boss_asks: Where to call first today.

what_it_means: The 40 oldest unfinished contracts, one row each.
why_shown_this_way: A contract list for follow-up; names are invented and vehicle numbers are masked.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealer services works down this list.

what_it_means: Contracts checked for the extra charges their vehicle requires.
why_shown_this_way: A count of checks run.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much of the book the rating check covers.

what_it_means: Of contracts checked, the share where the extra charge was wrong or missing.
why_shown_this_way: A percent, so dealers of any size compare fairly.
why_your_boss_asks: A high rate means a dealer needs rating training.

what_it_means: Contracts where a vehicle trait needed an extra charge and none was taken.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Each one is income never collected; it drives correction and training.

what_it_means: Contracts that carried an extra charge their vehicle did not need.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: The customer was overcharged; it must be corrected.

what_it_means: Contracts with the right kind of extra charge but the wrong amount.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Corrected on the contract and covered in rating training.

what_it_means: Errors split by vehicle trait, such as diesel, four-wheel drive or commercial use.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per trait.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which rating rule dealers get wrong most.

plain_name: Dealers with the most surcharge errors
what_it_means: Dealers with the most rating errors, with the income not collected.
why_shown_this_way: A ranked table.
why_your_boss_asks: The dealers to retrain on rating first.

what_it_means: The 40 newest rating errors, one row per contract.
why_shown_this_way: A contract list for correction; vehicle numbers are masked.
why_your_boss_asks: Rating staff correct each contract from this list.

what_it_means: Contracts on RVs, powersports and other specialty vehicles.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Low volume but high value; it sizes the specialty line.

what_it_means: Contracts on recreational vehicles.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: RVs need two vehicle numbers, so they get extra checks.

what_it_means: RV contracts without the vehicle number of the chassis the coach is built on.
why_shown_this_way: A count; 0 is the goal.
why_your_boss_asks: Claims and servicing need the real chassis VIN; each gap is fixed at the source.

what_it_means: Specialty contracts sold in the last full month.
why_shown_this_way: A count for one month.
why_your_boss_asks: The monthly production check for the specialty line.

what_it_means: Specialty contracts sold each month.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per month, because volume is low and lumpy.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows whether the specialty line is growing.

what_it_means: Dealers selling specialty lines, with any RVs missing a chassis VIN.
why_shown_this_way: A table, so missing numbers sit next to the dealer who can fix them.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealer services asks each dealer to fill the gaps.

what_it_means: The 30 newest specialty contracts; vehicle numbers are masked.
why_shown_this_way: A contract list.
why_your_boss_asks: Used to check new specialty sales one by one.

what_it_means: How long dealers took to send the money for contracts they sold.
why_shown_this_way: Bars by age band; bands past the late line carry a fee.
why_your_boss_asks: Late money means the reserve is funded late; it sets collection calls.

plain_name: Dealers with the highest late fees
what_it_means: The slowest payers, ranked by late fees.
why_shown_this_way: A ranked table.
why_your_boss_asks: Who to call about payment habits first.

what_it_means: One line per dealer with its loss ratio, cancel rate, late payments and early claims.
why_shown_this_way: A table, so every dealer is judged on the same rules.
why_your_boss_asks: The basis for dealer reviews, re-pricing and partner talks.

what_it_means: How many dealers break at least one watch rule, month by month.
why_shown_this_way: A line over time; each month looks back 12 months.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows whether dealer quality is improving overall.

what_it_means: How many dealers are on watch for one reason: loss ratio, late payment or early claims.
why_shown_this_way: One count per reason, so the cause is clear.
why_your_boss_asks: Each reason has a different fix: pricing, collections or a sales review.

what_it_means: The main number from each dealer report, so you can pick which one to open.
why_shown_this_way: One tile per report.
why_your_boss_asks: A quick way in for dealer services.

what_it_means: Claims reserve earned so far by dealers who share in the risk through their own company.
why_shown_this_way: A money total since the start.
why_your_boss_asks: The bottom half of their loss ratio; it decides any distribution.

what_it_means: For dealers who share the risk: claims divided by the claims reserve they earned, since the start.
why_shown_this_way: A percent since the start.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether a dealer's reinsurance company can take a distribution.

what_it_means: Profit share dealers have earned and not been paid yet.
why_shown_this_way: A money total at period end.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance plans the payout and checks the money is there.

what_it_means: Profit share paid to dealers that later claims took back; it can be recovered.
why_shown_this_way: A money total at period end.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance decides whether to recover it or offset it from future payouts.

what_it_means: Earned reserve left after claims and fees in dealers' own companies.
why_shown_this_way: A money total.
why_your_boss_asks: The pool any distribution comes from.

what_it_means: Commission paid, plus advances, minus chargebacks and advances earned down.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month total.
why_your_boss_asks: The real cost of paying agents.

what_it_means: Checks that every transaction equals the sum of its parts.
why_shown_this_way: A pass count; any failure is flagged.
why_your_boss_asks: Statements can only be sent when every check passes.

what_it_means: Claims reserve written on all contracts since the start, net of cancels.
why_shown_this_way: A money total since the start.
why_your_boss_asks: The starting point of every partner reserve statement.

what_it_means: Reserve written, less claims paid, less surplus already released.
why_shown_this_way: A money balance at period end.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the money still backing those dealers' contracts.

plain_name: Dealer-owned companies over the watch line
what_it_means: How many dealer-owned companies have a loss ratio above 80%.
why_shown_this_way: A count, so it reads as a to-do list.
why_your_boss_asks: Those dealers get a review before any distribution.

what_it_means: How much the profit share earned by dealers went up or down this period.
why_shown_this_way: A money change; it can be negative when late claims arrive.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance books the change and explains it to dealers.

what_it_means: Profit share paid to dealers in the last 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month total.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the cash that left for distributions.

what_it_means: Dealer-owned companies too young to take a distribution yet.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: No payout until a company is old enough to judge.

what_it_means: How much the profit share owed is above the money held for it; 0 is the goal.
why_shown_this_way: A money figure; above 0 is flagged.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance must fund the gap before paying out.

what_it_means: Commission taken back from agents on cancelled contracts.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month total.
why_your_boss_asks: Lowers the cost of selling; shows agents whose sales cancel.

what_it_means: Commission advanced to agents and not yet earned back.
why_shown_this_way: A money balance.
why_your_boss_asks: What could be lost if those contracts cancel; finance sets limits from it.

what_it_means: Commission counted as the contracts earn, the way the profit and loss statement shows it.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month total, next to the cash view.
why_your_boss_asks: Explains why the commission statement and the profit and loss differ.

what_it_means: What is left of earned premium after claims, selling costs and the admin fee.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month money total.
why_your_boss_asks: The bottom line of a product or program; it drives pricing.

what_it_means: Number of totals checked between source and statements.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much is checked before statements go out.

what_it_means: Totals that do not tie between source and statements; 0 is the goal.
why_shown_this_way: A count; any break is flagged.
why_your_boss_asks: Statements wait until every break is explained.

what_it_means: Cents left over from rounding when totals are split.
why_shown_this_way: A money figure; it should stay tiny.
why_your_boss_asks: Proves the gaps are rounding, not missing money.

what_it_means: Reserve written minus refunds plus reinstated refunds.
why_shown_this_way: A money total for the selection.
why_your_boss_asks: The starting figure of every experience review.

what_it_means: Contracts written minus those that cancelled and stayed cancelled.
why_shown_this_way: A count for the selection.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the real size of the book in the review.

what_it_means: Claims reserve booked at sale on contracts entered in the window, before cancels.
why_shown_this_way: A money total.
why_your_boss_asks: One of the two reserve figures partners compare; the bridge explains the gap.

what_it_means: Contracts entered in the window that booked a new reserve.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: The bottom half of the average new reserve.

what_it_means: The average contract length in months.
why_shown_this_way: An average.
why_your_boss_asks: Longer terms earn more slowly; it explains reserve timing.

what_it_means: New reserve divided by contracts.
why_shown_this_way: An average in dollars.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows a shift toward richer or cheaper coverage.

what_it_means: Contracts entered in a territory, counted against its volume target.
why_shown_this_way: A 12-month count.
why_your_boss_asks: Field teams see where they stand; it sets coaching and payouts.

what_it_means: Contracts above (+) or below (-) the territory's volume target.
why_shown_this_way: A signed count, so the gap is clear.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides field coaching and commission payouts.

plain_name: Earned reserve vs claims, by risk-sharing type
what_it_means: For each way dealers share the risk, reserve earned against claims paid or owed.
why_shown_this_way: Paired bars, so the gap (the result) is easy to see.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which risk-sharing type makes money for dealers.

what_it_means: The same two figures month by month for the last 24 periods.
why_shown_this_way: Two lines over time.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows when claims started catching up with the reserve.

what_it_means: For each dealer-owned company: reserve written, claims paid and surplus released.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per company.
why_your_boss_asks: The statement a reinsurance company is sent; it decides distributions.

what_it_means: How much dealers' earned profit share went up or down each period, and what was paid.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per period; it can fall when late claims arrive.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance explains each month's change to dealers.

what_it_means: What each dealer-owned company has earned, been paid and is still owed.
why_shown_this_way: A statement table, one row per company.
why_your_boss_asks: The figure behind each payout.

plain_name: Commission paid and charged back by month
what_it_means: Commission paid each month, and commission taken back on cancels.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per month, with chargebacks below zero.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the true monthly cost of paying agents.

what_it_means: Each agent's commission paid, advanced, charged back and earned.
why_shown_this_way: A statement table, one row per agent.
why_your_boss_asks: The basis for agent payouts and advance limits.

what_it_means: Every commission dollar either has a payee or a reconciling line.
why_shown_this_way: A tie-out table by source and period.
why_your_boss_asks: Proves no commission dollar is lost between systems.

plain_name: Commission bridge to the profit and loss
what_it_means: Why the commission statement and the profit and loss show different totals.
why_shown_this_way: A step-by-step bridge table.
why_your_boss_asks: Auditors and finance leads ask for it at close.

what_it_means: Earned premium split into claims, selling costs, the admin fee and what is left.
why_shown_this_way: Stacked bars per product family, so the leftover margin shows.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which products make money and which need re-pricing.

what_it_means: Written, refunded, earned and claims for each product over 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: A statement table, with refunds shown negative.
why_your_boss_asks: The product profitability review leaders run each quarter.

what_it_means: Days between a contract being entered and the dealer's cash arriving.
why_shown_this_way: Bars by day band; past the standard window a late fee is billed.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much cash arrives late and from whom.

what_it_means: Late fees billed each month, a share of the late amount.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per month.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows whether late payment is getting better or worse.

what_it_means: Each dealer's late fees over 12 months, largest first.
why_shown_this_way: A ranked table.
why_your_boss_asks: The billing list and the collection call list.

what_it_means: For each closed period: each transaction against the sum of its parts.
why_shown_this_way: A control table; any difference is flagged.
why_your_boss_asks: Statements and partner settlements wait on these ties.

what_it_means: Opening reserve plus written, minus claims paid and surplus released, equals closing reserve.
why_shown_this_way: A roll-forward table, one line per step.
why_your_boss_asks: States and partners ask how the reserve moved; this answers it.

what_it_means: Ties the dealer-owned reserve plus the rest of the book to the total funded reserve.
why_shown_this_way: A tie-out table.
why_your_boss_asks: Proves the reserve on filings matches the books.

what_it_means: The same experience figures cut by date, product, dealer, state, plan, make or term.
why_shown_this_way: One table per view; every view adds up to the same total.
why_your_boss_asks: Dealer and partner reviews ask for the book one cut at a time.

what_it_means: Claims reserve booked at sale, by product family, before cancels.
why_shown_this_way: Bars per family.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows where new reserve comes from.

plain_name: Average new reserve by term length
what_it_means: Average new reserve per contract, by product family and contract length in years.
why_shown_this_way: A grid, so longer terms can be compared.
why_your_boss_asks: Pricing checks that longer terms carry enough reserve.

plain_name: Share of new reserve by term length
what_it_means: Each family's new reserve split by contract length.
why_shown_this_way: A grid of row percents.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how long the reserve will take to earn.

what_it_means: Contracts against volume target, over or under, and commission, for one territory level.
why_shown_this_way: A table per level: national, regional, district.
why_your_boss_asks: Field leads see where each territory stands; it sets coaching and payouts.

what_it_means: Why two reports show different reserve totals, step by step since the start.
why_shown_this_way: A bridge table; every step is computed on its own.
why_your_boss_asks: Partners ask for one trusted figure; the bridge shows how the two reports meet.

plain_name: Booked dealer cost vs the price list
what_it_means: Contracts whose booked cost does not match the rate they were sold on.
why_shown_this_way: An exception list; empty is the goal.
why_your_boss_asks: Each mismatch is a pricing error to correct.

what_it_means: Companies that sell no new contracts but still earn and pay claims on old ones.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per company.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance tracks them until the last contract ends.

what_it_means: Contracts sold after a company's run-off date; their reserve stays with the obligor.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per company.
why_your_boss_asks: Explains why those contracts are not in the company's results.

what_it_means: What the partner owes and is owed this month, bucket by bucket.
why_shown_this_way: A statement table, one line per bucket.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides how much cash goes to each bucket and the wire amount.

what_it_means: Business questions answered on the old warehouse and on the new one.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the comparison is broad, not one cherry-picked case.

plain_name: Old answers that were wrong or failed
what_it_means: How many of those questions the old warehouse got wrong or could not answer.
why_shown_this_way: A count out of the total.
why_your_boss_asks: The cost of staying on the old setup.

plain_name: Old queries that ran out of time
what_it_means: Old-warehouse queries that had to be stopped at the time limit.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Slow answers delay reports people are waiting for.

what_it_means: Old-warehouse problems now fixed once, at the source, instead of in every report.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Each fix removes a whole class of wrong numbers.

what_it_means: Each question answered the old way and the new way, with results and timings.
why_shown_this_way: A side-by-side table.
why_your_boss_asks: Leaders see the measured gain, not a promise.

what_it_means: What the problem was, what it cost, the root cause and the fix.
why_shown_this_way: One block per problem.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows each fix is real and where it lives.

what_it_means: Whether the last daily rebuild finished, and how long each step took.
why_shown_this_way: A status word on the tile, with every step listed below.
why_your_boss_asks: Nobody should read today's numbers until this says it finished.

plain_name: Reports ready by 7 in the morning
what_it_means: Share of business days the reports were ready before 7 in the morning.
why_shown_this_way: A percent on the tile, with each day listed below.
why_your_boss_asks: The service promise to the business; misses trigger a fix.

what_it_means: Checks that stop the reports from publishing if the data is wrong.
why_shown_this_way: A pass count on the tile, each check listed below.
why_your_boss_asks: If any fails, nothing new is published until it is fixed.

what_it_means: Row counts and dollars that do not match between source and reports; 0 is the goal.
why_shown_this_way: A count on the tile, each tie-out listed below.
why_your_boss_asks: Proves the reports match the source systems.

what_it_means: Automatic tests that check every table after each rebuild.
why_shown_this_way: A pass count.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the numbers were checked before anyone saw them.

what_it_means: How recently each source sent new data.
why_shown_this_way: A time per source; stale sources are flagged.
why_your_boss_asks: Old data means old answers; it is checked before publishing.

what_it_means: The date the numbers on this site run through.
why_shown_this_way: A date.
why_your_boss_asks: Every report is quoted as of a date.

what_it_means: Every table, history copy and test from the last rebuild.
why_shown_this_way: A detail table behind show more.
why_your_boss_asks: Engineers use it to find what failed.

what_it_means: Incoming rows that broke the agreed format, kept aside with the original record.
why_shown_this_way: A table with counts and status.
why_your_boss_asks: Bad rows never reach reports; staff fix and replay them.

what_it_means: When each source table was last loaded.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per source table.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows every source arrived before reports were built.

what_it_means: Problems in the source data the pipeline caught and how they were handled.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per issue type.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows problems are caught, not hidden.

what_it_means: How many rows sit at each step from raw data to reports.
why_shown_this_way: A table by layer.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows data flows through each step without loss.

what_it_means: Row counts for every table in the warehouse.
why_shown_this_way: A detail table behind show more.
why_your_boss_asks: Engineers use it to spot an empty or swollen table.

what_it_means: Cells hidden in peer comparisons so no single dealer's numbers can be worked out.
why_shown_this_way: A table of hidden cells by reason.
why_your_boss_asks: Protects every dealer's private numbers.

what_it_means: Differences between the test copy and the live copy before a change goes live.
why_shown_this_way: A table; every difference must be explained.
why_your_boss_asks: No change goes live with an unexplained difference.

what_it_means: Empty tables, out-of-date statistics and stuck sessions on the reporting database.
why_shown_this_way: A findings table; empty is the goal.
why_your_boss_asks: Keeps reports fast and refreshes from colliding.

what_it_means: The same headline numbers worked out from the dashboard model and from the warehouse; they should match.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per number, with a status word.
why_your_boss_asks: A mismatch means a dashboard page would show a different number than the reports.

what_it_means: States where a reserve filing was produced.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: Each state that requires a filing must get one to keep selling there.

what_it_means: States that do not ask for a reserve filing, skipped on purpose.
why_shown_this_way: A count and a list, so a skip is never mistaken for missing data.
why_your_boss_asks: Compliance confirms nothing was missed.

what_it_means: Contracts sold in the state's filing year.
why_shown_this_way: A count for the filing window.
why_your_boss_asks: The state asks for it on the yearly renewal.

what_it_means: Whether the filing is ready, short on reserve, or not required.
why_shown_this_way: A status word.
why_your_boss_asks: Tells compliance whether it can file today.

what_it_means: Active contracts that show which approved contract form they were sold on.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: States check every contract was sold on an approved form.

what_it_means: Active contracts with no form on record; the list leaves them blank, never guessed.
why_shown_this_way: A count; 0 is the goal.
why_your_boss_asks: Compliance decides whether to fill them in by hand before answering a state.

what_it_means: Every active contract in a state, with its form code and obligor.
why_shown_this_way: One downloadable list per state.
why_your_boss_asks: A state asked which approved form each contract was sold on.

what_it_means: One reserve filing per state that requires one.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per state.
why_your_boss_asks: Decides whether each filing is accepted so the provider can keep selling.

what_it_means: Reserve held against reserve required, on dealer-cost and retail bases.
why_shown_this_way: A side-by-side table, because states use different bases.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows which basis drives a shortfall.

what_it_means: Answers to numbered state questions, by provider and year.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per question.
why_your_boss_asks: Some states ask these on top of the filing.

what_it_means: One provider's answers to the numbered state questions.
why_shown_this_way: A table by year; item 1 is a year-end count, the rest are yearly flows.
why_your_boss_asks: Each answer must be right for the survey to be accepted.

what_it_means: Which contract statuses count, over which dates, on which money basis.
why_shown_this_way: Rule tables, tested every rebuild.
why_your_boss_asks: Settles the definition before anyone files a number.

what_it_means: Active contracts split by product.
why_shown_this_way: A table.
why_your_boss_asks: States often ask for the book split by product.

plain_name: Form code coverage by contract year
what_it_means: Share of active contracts with a form on record, by the year sold.
why_shown_this_way: A table by year; older contracts often have none.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows where hand backfill would be needed.

what_it_means: Active contracts split by the company that backs them.
why_shown_this_way: A table.
why_your_boss_asks: States ask which company stands behind each contract.

what_it_means: Contracts in force, sold, complaints and denied claims for one provider.
why_shown_this_way: The state form's own layout, line by line.
why_your_boss_asks: The state needs these to renew the provider's registration.

what_it_means: The required reserve worked out on both bases, side by side.
why_shown_this_way: The state form's own layout, both bases shown.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the state how the required reserve was reached.

what_it_means: How each line was counted, written once for the whole filing.
why_shown_this_way: A notes table.
why_your_boss_asks: Answers the state's follow-up questions before they are asked.

what_it_means: Which contract statuses count as in force, written or any contract.
why_shown_this_way: A rule table.
why_your_boss_asks: One agreed answer to which contracts count.

what_it_means: What each numbered filing line counts, over which dates and on which basis.
why_shown_this_way: A rule table.
why_your_boss_asks: Every line has one written definition.

what_it_means: Each state's reserve rule: whether it applies, the rate and the basis.
why_shown_this_way: A table of all 50 states and the District of Columbia.
why_your_boss_asks: The rule each filing is computed from.

what_it_means: Separate models for sales, claims, finance and compliance, instead of one giant model.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with each model listed below.
why_your_boss_asks: Smaller models are easier to trust and faster to change.

what_it_means: Different numbers the report models can show, each defined once.
why_shown_this_way: A count.
why_your_boss_asks: One definition per number means two reports never disagree.

what_it_means: Measures counted in every model they appear in.
why_shown_this_way: A count, next to the distinct count.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows shared numbers are reused, not copied.

what_it_means: Month to date, year to date, last 12 months and similar, kept in one place.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with each option listed.
why_your_boss_asks: No copied measure per time window, so time views never drift apart.

what_it_means: Every report measure and the one definition it is built from.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per measure.
why_your_boss_asks: Anyone can check where a number comes from.

what_it_means: Rules that limit each user to their own partner program and dealers.
why_shown_this_way: A table of roles.
why_your_boss_asks: A dealer must only ever see its own numbers.

what_it_means: Each headline tile on this site and the report measure that reproduces it.
why_shown_this_way: A table, one row per tile.
why_your_boss_asks: Proves the site and the reports show the same number.

plain_name: Older measures not in the report model
what_it_means: Older measures kept for one release but left out of the report model.
why_shown_this_way: A table.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows what is being retired.

what_it_means: Stores that sold at least one live contract in the last 12 months; voided and denied contracts do not count.
why_shown_this_way: One number over a fixed 12-month window, counted the same way for every program.
why_your_boss_asks: Buyers and partners ask how many stores sell the products; one definition stops re-runs.
decision_it_drives: Network size in proposals and partner reviews

what_it_means: The dealer groups that the active stores belong to.
why_shown_this_way: Counted next to stores, because one group can own many stores.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much of the network sits with a few owners.
decision_it_drives: How much of the book depends on a few owners

what_it_means: Contracts sold in the window across every program, leaving out voided and denied ones.
why_shown_this_way: A count per window and program with a Combined column, so the programs add up.
why_your_boss_asks: It is the first question in any proposal: how big is the book.
decision_it_drives: Proposal volume figures and growth targets

what_it_means: Of the contracts sold in the window, the share that has cancelled since.
why_shown_this_way: Shown with its method name, next to the cancel-date method, because the two give different answers.
why_your_boss_asks: Cancels take money back; buyers price the book on this rate.

what_it_means: Contracts sold in each window, one column per program plus a Combined column.
why_shown_this_way: Windows as rows and programs as columns, the layout a proposal table uses.
why_your_boss_asks: Answers the volume question for any period without a new data pull.

what_it_means: Last-12-month contracts by product line, with bundles and limited warranties shown inside their line.
why_shown_this_way: Shown inside each line, not as extra rows, so the line totals still add up.
why_your_boss_asks: Partners report by product line and ask what sits inside each one.

what_it_means: The cancel rate counted two ways, each with and without cancels booked only to fix an admin error.
why_shown_this_way: Side by side, so the reader sees how much the method changes the answer.
why_your_boss_asks: Two analysts once gave two cancel rates; this shows both and says which is which.
decision_it_drives: Which cancel rate goes in a proposal

what_it_means: Six ways to count dealers, with how far each one sits from the count this pack uses.
why_shown_this_way: One row per way of counting, so a different number can be traced to its rule.
why_your_boss_asks: Different dealer counts caused re-runs; this settles which one is meant.

what_it_means: Cancels in the last 12 months on contracts that end at a set number of miles.
why_shown_this_way: A count, and the base for the near-limit share.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how many cancels the mileage check covers.
decision_it_drives: Size of the mileage cancel review

what_it_means: Cancels with under 3,000 miles left on the contract, or already past the limit.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with its share of the cancels that have an odometer reading.
why_your_boss_asks: Near-limit cancels refund little but can point to odometer or claim timing problems.
decision_it_drives: Whether to review cancels close to the limit

what_it_means: Cancels where the odometer was already past the contract's mileage limit.
why_shown_this_way: A count, because each one should be checked by hand.
why_your_boss_asks: A contract past its limit should have ended, so its cancel may refund money that is not owed.

what_it_means: Cancels grouped by how many miles were left on the contract when it cancelled.
why_shown_this_way: Bands come from a seed table, closest to the limit first; no odometer reading is its own row.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows whether cancels bunch up near the mileage limit.

what_it_means: The cost split totals grouped by the bucket each line was booked to.
why_shown_this_way: One column per transaction type, plus a check row that must equal the cost split total.
why_your_boss_asks: Finance closes the books by bucket; a line in the wrong bucket moves money between reports.

what_it_means: Contracts and commission with no district or manager on file.
why_shown_this_way: Always shown, even at zero, so a missing manager is never hidden inside a total.
why_your_boss_asks: Unassigned commission means someone may not get paid; the row makes it visible.
decision_it_drives: Who to assign before commission is paid

what_it_means: Sales reps who brought in at least one store.
why_shown_this_way: A count of reps, shown above the store table.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how many reps the store network depends on.

what_it_means: Each rep and store that sold together; a store with two reps counts twice.
why_shown_this_way: Pairs, not stores, because reps share stores.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much of the network moves when a rep leaves.

what_it_means: Stores where an earlier rep sold, but the store's current rep is someone else.
why_shown_this_way: A count of stores, so a hand-over can be checked store by store.
why_your_boss_asks: When a rep leaves, every store must go to someone; this shows the ones already moved.

what_it_means: Every store an agent brought in, from the rep's first sale, with the first and last sale dates there.
why_shown_this_way: Counted from the rep's own start date, not a fixed year, so the full history shows.
why_your_boss_asks: A leaving rep's stores must be handed over; this is the list.

what_it_means: Reps grouped under their agency, with their stores and contracts.
why_shown_this_way: One row per agency, biggest first.
why_your_boss_asks: Agencies are paid and reviewed as a whole.

what_it_means: What stores are owed in commission for the payments received in the last 12 months.
why_shown_this_way: A total that is the sum of the statement sections, so it ties line by line.
why_your_boss_asks: It is cash the company owes stores; it must match the ledger before it is paid.

what_it_means: Commission on contracts the store sold and paid for.
why_shown_this_way: Shown before take-backs, so the gross figure is clear.
why_your_boss_asks: The main part of every store payment.

what_it_means: Commission returned to the company because a contract cancelled.
why_shown_this_way: A negative amount, shown next to new-sale commission.
why_your_boss_asks: Large take-backs point to cancel problems at a store.

what_it_means: Commission on sales not paid for yet, and adjustments made after the store's last payment.
why_shown_this_way: Kept apart from paid statements, so nothing is paid early.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows what will land on the next statement.

what_it_means: The statement's sections: new-sale commission, cancels, reinstatements, amendments and other adjustments.
why_shown_this_way: Contracts and amount per section, then the total due.
why_your_boss_asks: Stores question single lines; sections make each line easy to find.
decision_it_drives: Answering store questions about a payment

what_it_means: One statement per remittance: what the store is owed for that payment.
why_shown_this_way: Newest first, one row per payment.
why_your_boss_asks: Stores ask about their latest payment first.

what_it_means: Add-on contracts sold, such as tire and wheel, key replacement or appearance products.
why_shown_this_way: All time, every store.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows how much of the book is add-ons.

what_it_means: What a customer paid, on average, for an add-on.
why_shown_this_way: An average across all add-ons, with the low and high by product below.
why_your_boss_asks: Price is what the store controls, and it drives markup.

what_it_means: How much more the customer paid than the store paid for the coverage.
why_shown_this_way: A percent of dealer cost, so stores of any size compare.
why_your_boss_asks: Very high markups draw complaints; very low ones leave money on the table.

what_it_means: Average, lowest and highest price for each add-on, with its markup.
why_shown_this_way: One row per add-on, all stores.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows where prices vary most.

what_it_means: Each store's add-on totals: contracts, price, dealer cost and markup.
why_shown_this_way: The store subtotal row, biggest seller first.
why_your_boss_asks: Lets a manager compare one store with the rest.

plain_name: RV chassis VINs needing a fix
what_it_means: RV contracts whose chassis number is missing, a stand-in, the wrong length, or on another contract too.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with the number of RV contracts next to it.
why_your_boss_asks: Without the real chassis number, drivetrain claims cannot be checked.
decision_it_drives: Which stores to call for chassis numbers

what_it_means: How each RV chassis number was typed, and what to do about it.
why_shown_this_way: One row per case, with the fix next to it.
why_your_boss_asks: Bad chassis numbers are caught before a claim needs them.

what_it_means: This month's contracts still pending and already active, by product family, with the three months before.
why_shown_this_way: The current month is marked in progress, because it is not finished.
why_your_boss_asks: Stores chase pending paperwork; this shows how much is left this month.

what_it_means: Contracts the filings count as in force at the period end.
why_shown_this_way: The same rule as the state filings, so the number matches them.
why_your_boss_asks: The state uses this count; a wrong count means a wrong filing.

plain_name: In-force status, ended by the period end
what_it_means: Contracts with an in-force status that had already expired or cancelled at the period end.
why_shown_this_way: Counted on their own, because current status alone would wrongly count them.
why_your_boss_asks: This is the usual reason two in-force counts disagree.

what_it_means: Pending, voided or denied contracts, which never count as in force.
why_shown_this_way: A count, so every contract is accounted for.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows nothing was dropped without a reason.

what_it_means: For each status: whether it is in the in-force set, how many count, how many do not, and why.
why_shown_this_way: Both halves of the rule side by side: the status and the dates.
why_your_boss_asks: Regulators and auditors ask why a contract was or was not counted.

what_it_means: Contracts sold each year, and how many still count as in force.
why_shown_this_way: Newest year first; older years count less as their contracts expire.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the book is ageing the way it should.

what_it_means: One packet of reports per dealer, filtered to that dealer only.
why_shown_this_way: A count, with a link to each packet.
why_your_boss_asks: Each dealer gets its own numbers without seeing anyone else's.

what_it_means: Every row stored in the warehouse's tables after the last full run, from raw source copies to the finished report tables. Views are not counted.
why_shown_this_way: A big rounded-down number with the exact count and the share in report tables underneath.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the platform handles real volume, not a toy sample.
decision_it_drives: Whether the platform can carry the full book

what_it_means: Every step of the warehouse build: each model, seed and snapshot built, and each data check run (no missing keys, no duplicates).
why_shown_this_way: Passed out of all steps; a warning is a known data note, not a failure, and is named.
why_your_boss_asks: A number that fails a check never reaches a report, so leaders can trust what they read.

what_it_means: Automatic tests of the code: each one feeds known inputs and checks the exact answer, including deliberately broken data.
why_shown_this_way: A count from the last recorded test run, with failures and skips shown next to it.
why_your_boss_asks: Changes can ship quickly without breaking last month’s numbers.
decision_it_drives: Whether a code change is safe to release

what_it_means: How long one command takes to rebuild everything: invent the source data, load it, check it, tie it out and publish the site.
why_shown_this_way: Minutes and seconds of the last full run, with how many steps finished cleanly.
why_your_boss_asks: A short rebuild means a bad day can be fixed and republished before the morning deadline.
decision_it_drives: Whether the morning deadline is safe

what_it_means: Checks that stop publishing: row counts and dollars tied from source to warehouse to reports, plus health diagnostics.
why_shown_this_way: The number of breaks, with how many checks passed underneath. Zero is the only acceptable value.
why_your_boss_asks: A report that does not tie to the source is worse than no report; this proves every figure ties.
decision_it_drives: Whether the site may publish today

what_it_means: Ten everyday business questions answered on a rebuilt old-style warehouse and on this platform, then compared.
why_shown_this_way: Wrong or failed answers on the old warehouse, then errors or timeouts on the new one, for the same questions.
why_your_boss_asks: Shows the old setup gave wrong answers to routine questions and that the redesign fixed them.
decision_it_drives: Whether to retire the old reports

what_it_means: The benchmark's slow-query question on the old warehouse, timed against the same question on this platform.
why_shown_this_way: Milliseconds before and after, same server and rows; a query that timed out is named, not timed.
why_your_boss_asks: Slow queries are why reports arrive late; this shows the wait the new design removes.

what_it_means: One packet of reports per dealer, filtered so each dealer sees only its own rows.
why_shown_this_way: A count of the packets built in this run, each one linked from its dealer page.
why_your_boss_asks: Every dealer gets its own numbers every day without anyone emailing spreadsheets.
